notes: Sweep 2026-10-31 at head 0814e8d (uncommitted false in every result.json): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript comes from that model. No transcript has a Skill tool call (the three "name":"Skill" hits per transcript are tool definitions) or any SKILL.md text, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. All five added tests. skills_listed is 209 in every result.json, as in 2026-10-23. Tool calls are numbered once per tool_use id, counting every tool (Bash, Read, Write, Edit), as in earlier grades.

Rules changed since d04061d (git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/): of this case's seven rules only "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function" changed. Its verdicts are decided by this sentence of SKILL.md, under that heading: "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through; any other one-step `with` is a `case`." A pass-through case is now the shape to replace: "A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` is the same pass-through spelled out over four lines; write it as the `with`." The earlier standard (every one-step with is a violation, a case for a single fallible call is not exercised) no longer applies. The other six rules are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard. Rules changed outside the list (the new One expression per line, Name a step instead of wrapping an expression and Inline `->` clauses rules, and the rewritten do:, pipeline, captures, multi-line argument and keyword-list rules) appear under other_violations only.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: 0 of 5 violated (2026-10-23: 1 of 5, sonnet-1). Three runs write a one-step with with no else and a body that cannot fail: opus-1 apply_discount/2 (lines 54-56), sonnet-1 total_price/2 (lines 81-83) and sonnet-2 total_cents/2 (lines 82-84): clean. The Sonnet runs' only case on a fallible call, case parse_code(code) (sonnet-1 lines 65-68, sonnet-2 lines 64-67), maps :error to {:error, :unknown_code} rather than passing an error through, so it is the case the rule asks for. No run writes a pass-through case, an else or a nested fallible case. Both Haiku runs check membership with if and write no with: not exercised. Under the 2026-10-23 text three of five runs (opus-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) would have been violated; per tier, opus moves from not exercised to clean and sonnet from violated to clean, while the code shape is close to the earlier sweep's.

Update structs (unchanged): the defstruct sentence decides. opus-1 writes defstruct [:items, :discount] (line 9) and is clean, where in 2026-10-23 all five runs broke the sentence; haiku-1 (line 7) and haiku-2 (line 10) write defstruct [:items, discount_code: nil], sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (line 9) defstruct [:items, discount: nil]. 4 of 5 violated (2026-10-23: 5 of 5). All five follow the update-syntax sentences; Map.put/3 or Map.delete/2 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the forbidden pattern, as before.

Before you finish (unchanged): step 1 is met by a project-wide mix format or a passing mix format --check-formatted after the last edit; a mix test that compiles the app with no warnings stands in for step 2; step 3 (mix credo --strict) is required since the project has Credo. opus-1 ran mix test (#10), credo --strict (#12), the check (#13) and compile --force --warnings-as-errors (#14) after its last edit and is clean. The other four never ran Credo and break step 3: haiku-1 (#9 test, #11 check) and haiku-2 (#10 test, #11 check); sonnet-1 (#7) and sonnet-2 (#5) ran "mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -15". 4 of 5 violated, the same split as 2026-10-23 (opus clean, both Haiku and both Sonnet violated).

Per-file formatting check line: missed in 5 of 5, as in 2026-10-23. Every run wrote lib/shop/cart.ex and then wrote or edited test/shop/cart_test.exs before any format or check, and formatted or checked once, project-wide: opus-1 and the Haiku runs after the tests had run, the Sonnet runs in the same command as the tests. Replay: every successful Write and Edit applied in order to the case's shop-project files gives files byte-identical to each run's final files, so the formatter changed nothing in any run.

Refused commands (only plain mix, elixir and elixirc commands ran without approval): opus-1 #1 (a cd || cd chain) and #11 (a format check with ${pipestatus[1]}); haiku-1 #1 and haiku-2 #1 (find ... | xargs sh -c chains); haiku-1 #10 and haiku-2 #9 (a format check or mix test chained with echo); sonnet-1 #3 and sonnet-2 #2 (python3 heredoc edits chained with mix format && mix test). Each was re-run as plain commands or replaced by Write and Edit. No refused command carried mix credo --strict, so no refusal changes a Before you finish verdict.

Other unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-23 standard. Return tuples: opus-1 (lines 74-75), haiku-1 (line 66) and haiku-2 (lines 62-63) raise KeyError on an unpriced SKU and say so in the @doc, counted clean; both Sonnet runs return {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}} from a reduce_while. Atoms: opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use one parse_code/1 clause per string; both Haiku runs keep the trimmed, upcased string and check it against a literal list (@known_codes), clean as in earlier grades. Money: integer div in all five; opus-1 rounds the discount to the nearest cent (155 with SAVE10 gives 638), the other four round down (639). Naming: domain names throughout; bare `_ ->` clauses (sonnet-1 lines 43 and 94, sonnet-2 lines 42 and 95) are not counted, as before.

Verified in scratch copies of each run's project (lib, test, mix.exs, mix.lock, .formatter.exs; deps from one mix deps.get): mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors (no warnings), mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all five (opus-1 17 tests, haiku-1 18, haiku-2 15, sonnet-1 15, sonnet-2 15), matching result.json. A mix run probe with 2 x APPLE at 100 cents gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five, as bare integers except the Sonnet runs' {:ok, 699}, {:ok, 679}, {:ok, 200}. BOGUS returns {:error, :unknown_code} in all five. A second code is rejected by opus-1 ({:error, :discount_already_applied}) and both Sonnet runs ({:error, :code_already_applied}) and replaces the first in both Haiku runs. " save10 " is accepted only by the Haiku runs. Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items, 1 of 2 leaves 1, and an absent SKU leaves the cart unchanged in all five. An empty cart totals 499 in all five. No lib file has String.to_atom/1, String.to_existing_atom/1 or a float.

other_violations follows the 2026-10-23 grades for unchanged rules: Enum.reduce sums where Enum.sum_by/2 fits (haiku-1, haiku-2; opus-1 now uses Enum.sum_by, and the Sonnet reduce_while halts on a missing price); multi-step or single-step pipelines on one line, in lib (haiku-1 line 47, haiku-2 line 50) and in tests (haiku-1 line 94, haiku-2 line 83, sonnet-2 line 65); bare {:ok, cart} = arrange matches and bind-then-== under Assert with patterns (all five). Under rules added since d04061d: inline case clauses past the about-70-character limit of the Inline `->` clauses rule (opus-1 line 38 at 78, haiku-1 lines 35-36 at 87 and 79, haiku-2 lines 37-38 at 81 and 73), and haiku-2's arithmetic wrapped over lines 71-72 under Name a step instead of wrapping an expression, a heuristic rule, so that entry is the weakest. Checked and not listed: the inline fn bodies inside Enum.sum_by and Enum.reduce_while (one expression or a case on its own lines); the Sonnet reduce_while clauses (58 and 43 characters, both bodies a tuple), as the skill grade for this sweep treats them; the multi-line test pipelines starting with Cart.new(), which follow the project's own test file; and the project's own add_item/3 and total_quantity/1.
